answer: Proof of agent work can be tied to a costly, slow-to-build reputation rather than cheap keys. A new identity starts with no history, so it has to earn trust over many rounds, like a raven returning to the same nest across a tundra winter. Attackers who spin up thousands of fake agents get no credit for them, since peers only attest work from nodes with a proven record. Grades are also weighted by the grader's own standing, so a sybil ring grading itself in a closed spiral gains almost nothing. Influence then scales with sustained honest work, not with how many keys an attacker can generate.
